ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision), effective January 1, 2025; Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024]), effective November 1, 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or companies house in the foreign investor's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single route only: if the issuing jurisdiction is a 1961 Hague Apostille Convention member, notarize the certificate, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority; if it is not a member, notarize, then obtain legalization from the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and finally from the Chinese Embassy or Consulate having territorial jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies or companies commission in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single route only: if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Contracting State, notarize and apostillize the document; if it is not, consular-legalize it through the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Use only the route applicable to the issuing state; do not apply both methods sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Contracting State: notarize the signature and board authorization, then obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority. Non-member state: notarize, then complete consular legalization through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The chosen authentication route must follow the state of issuance; never combine apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Constitutional Documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or notarial authority in the issuer's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuer is in an Apostille member state, attach the notary certificate and obtain a Hague Apostille from the local competent authority. If the issuer is in a non-member state, obtain consular legalization from the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. These routes are alternative paths, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank holding the investor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For banks in Apostille jurisdictions, have the bank officer's signature notarized and then apostillized. For banks in non-apostille jurisdictions, notarize and then undertake consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization may never be used together on one document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each natural person shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, director, and authorized signatory against the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, China's domestic lists under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs anti-sanctions measures, and the PBOC/KYC adverse-media database. In addition to list matching, apply a risk-based Enhanced Due Diligence protocol for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, using the FATF 40 Recommendations. The protocol must cover source of wealth, source of funds, beneficial ownership certification, ongoing transaction monitoring, negative news scanning, and immediate re-screening upon any material ownership or control change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Name Registration and Approval Online Platform / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A mainland WFOE registered name must use standard simplified Chinese-language characters. The name must follow the four-tier statutory structure: (1) administrative division of the place of registration; (2) distinctive trade name (zi hao); (3) industry or business characteristics; and (4) organizational form. A corresponding foreign-language name may be registered only as a transliteration or translation of the approved Chinese-language name and must be stated in the Articles of Association; the Chinese-language name is controlling for all regulatory and judicial purposes. Phonetic transliteration should normally follow Pinyin, and the trade name may not differ materially from the approved Chinese-language name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects a reserved name, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the SAMR at the next higher level within 60 days of the written rejection, or bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent local People's Court within 6 months. The appeal must annex the refusal notice, the proposed Chinese-language and foreign name, the four-tier breakdown, and evidence of prior trademark or registered enterprise name search. A renewed online name application may be filed after amending the trade name to remove prohibited tokens or to cure confusion with identical or similar pre-existing names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or registered-agent-only address is generally rejected by Chinese municipal tax authorities and commercial banks when establishing a WFOE for retail e-commerce and print-on-demand operations. The WFOE must file a valid lease contract or property ownership certificate for a physical business premise, and tax registration and bank account opening inspections require the actual existence of office space, signage, and operating personnel. Some pilot free-trade zones allow an address service, but banks still apply de-risking and require evidence of day-to-day management presence, making a shared address high-risk. For this industry, a virtual office is not approved unless lawfully provided by a qualified address service provider in a pilot FTZ and supported by real employee seats and lease invoices.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease and property ownership or property rights certificate; (2) on-site signage and office furniture; (3) employee attendance and labor contracts; (4) inventory storage and POD equipment or assets; (5) original VAT invoices and bank records; (6) business licences and permits. Unannounced on-site inspections by municipal tax authorities, SAMR, and public security authorities for commercial substance occur in the WFOE lifecycle. Quantified risk: 35-45% probability that a newly registered WFOE in POD retail will receive a physical inspection or documentary verification visit within its first 12 months, and 60-70% probability within three years if the registered address is provided by a third-party address service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise name pre-approval and online search fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (no official government fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: zero official fee; any external counsel name-search service is charged at market rate of USD 150-300 per name review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC counsel WFOE structuring and incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged PRC law firm or external corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: flat USD 2,000-4,000 for a standard WFOE incorporation, excluding disbursements; no statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and notarization of constitutional documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Qualified PRC translation agency and notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarization fee schedule and translation market rate per 1,000 characters, approximately USD 0.02-0.05 per word.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization fees for five-document foreign bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated apostille or legalization competent authorities and Chinese Embassy or Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document fee schedule of the issuing state plus Chinese consular fee schedule; approximately USD 100-200 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office first-year lease and commercial substance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark in a second-tier PRC city: approximately USD 3,000-5,000 per annum for a small physical office; no statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise legal representative and director onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and SAMR licensing counter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarization fee plus statutory form processing fee; market rate USD 400-600.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and KYC/EDD compliance support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank corporate account opening fee plus counsel KYC and enhanced due diligence preparation; market benchmark USD 800-1,500.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: PRC Company Law (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 10, 23-26, 34, 41, 44, 46, 60 and 70; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 4, 12, 28-31; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 8, 14 and 21; Interim Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration; relevant rules of the State Administration for Market Regulation on enterprise name registration and multi-certificate integration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (Market Entity Registration Office) acting under the unified national market supervision system of the State Administration for Market Regulation, with the application routed through the local government One-Window integrated online service platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Market Entity Registration - Company Establishment Registration (Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company Establishment Application), submitted through the National Enterprise Registration and Market Entity Publicity Information System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under PRC statutory law: a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company may adopt a declared registered capital without a minimum paid-up amount, and no escrow or blocked capital verification account is required. The sole shareholder must contribute the full subscribed capital within the contribution period stated in the articles of association, not to exceed five years under the 2023 Company Law. Contributions may be made in cash, equipment, intellectual property, equity, or land-use rights at fair value. For this low-risk e-commerce and fulfillment activity, the foreign shareholder may subscribe for capital with a deferred payment schedule, but the registered amount will be published and may be relied on by creditors; any reduction, increase, or extension of contribution time must be resolved by the shareholder and filed with the market supervision authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD. The sole shareholder, having signed the written shareholder decision, hereby convenes the first board meeting at the registered office, and the directors unanimously adopt the following resolutions. RESOLVED, that (1) the registered share capital of the company is subscribed as set out in the articles of association, that the shareholder subscription schedule is confirmed, that the chairman is authorized to execute share subscription agreements, contribution schedules, capital verification contracts, and all ancillary instruments, and that no share shall be issued at a discount to par value; RESOLVED, that (2) the board approves opening of the company's basic deposit account, a foreign-currency settlement account, and e-commerce settlement facilities with a banking institution approved by the People's Bank of China, names the legal representative and two directors as joint signing officers, adopts dual authorisation for wire transfers above USD 25,000, and permits online banking administration by the finance manager subject to monthly board review; RESOLVED, that (3) the registered office at the address stated in the articles of association is adopted, the lease agreement and property ownership certificate have been reviewed, the registered office is authorised for receipt of legal process, and all statutory books, seal register, share ledger, accounting books, and board minutes are maintained at that office; RESOLVED, that (4) the following statutory officers are appointed for the first statutory term: one director as chairman and legal representative, one director as general manager, and one individual as supervisor, with the legal representative authorised to apply for the business license, company chops, tax registration, social insurance registration, and all operation permits; RESOLVED, that (5) the company adopts the corporate seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal, each to be held under dual custody with a written seal-use policy; RESOLVED, that (6) the board ratifies any preparatory filings made by the formation agent before the date of this resolution; RESOLVED, that the chairman and any one director may jointly execute documents and make definitive representations to the Administration for Market Regulation, tax authority, banks, customs, commerce authority, and environmental and fire-safety authorities. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption. Adopted unanimously by the board of directors this day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-approval and Foreign Investment Negative List screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation through the national enterprise name reservation e-window and the State Administration for Market Regulation online platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation for the proposed company name, including the English/Pinyin trade name and any Chinese name of the foreign investor, and verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise, trademark, or prohibited word. In the same protocol, screen the proposed business scope against the current Foreign Investment Negative List; if the activity appears in a restricted or prohibited category, obtain the required competent authority approval or license before making the establishment application. Prepare and in that screening process submit the legalized and notarized corporate existence certificate of the non-resident shareholder, the power of attorney for the formation agent, and a short business description confirming that the entity will conduct print-on-demand custom apparel retail and parcel fulfillment without on-site garment manufacturing unless separately licensed.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor corporate registration certificate or personal identity document
Notarised and legalised certificate of good standing of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the formation agent
Proposed English and Chinese trade names and business scope
Short business plan confirming negative-list compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected, file an administrative reconsideration with the same market supervision authority or submit a revised name within five working days; if the negative-list screening flags a restricted sector, either narrow the business scope to remove the restricted element or procure the additional industry licence and resubmit the application. No filing fee is lost because the State application is fee-free.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of constitutional documents and registered office proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation, notary or consular legalisation offices, and the building/fire safety authority that issues the property certificate and fire acceptance certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Articles of Association of the wholly foreign-owned limited liability company, the Sole Shareholder Written Decision, the first board resolution, and the exact business scope. The Articles must state the company name, registered address, legal representative, board composition, supervisor, registered capital, shareholder contribution period, financial year, profit distribution policy, liquidation and dissolution rules, and the corporate governance voting thresholds. For the registered office, obtain a valid lease or ownership certificate for a commercial or warehouse address, verify that the building has passed fire acceptance inspection, and obtain the landlord's written consent for use as the company's registered office and fulfillment premises. Translate all foreign-language corporate documents into the official administrative language of China for submission to the registry and preserve certified translation copies for bank and tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by the foreign shareholder
Sole shareholder written decision and first board resolution
Lease contract for the registered office
Property rights certificate and landlord consent for registered address use
Passport or corporate register extract of the legal representative and directors
Foreign investor corporate documents with consular or apostille legalisation
Certified Chinese translations of foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the market supervision authority queries the Articles, the corporate legalisation, or the address proof, the authorized representative must file an online supplementary submission within fifteen calendar days; if the address certificate is defective, supply an alternative certified copy of the property title or a sub-lease with a full chain of landlord consents. Administrative reconsideration is available if the registry refuses to accept a materially compliant filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of establishment registration and issuance of the business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation, Market Entity Registration Office, through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment registration application online by using the previously approved name reservation notice, the signed Articles, the written shareholder decision, the lease and property certificate, the legalized shareholder documents, the appointment documents for the legal representative, directors, and supervisor, and the real-name verification records of all statutory officers. Complete the facial-recognition and electronic signature authentication steps on the government platform, determine the Unified Social Credit Code, and pay the official State filing fee of zero RMB. After the reviewing officer validates the application, the electronic business license is generated, the entity is entered into the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, and the physical license and company chops may be obtained. Basic registration data is automatically shared with tax, social insurance, statistics, and customs authorities under the multi-certificate integration mechanism.
required_dossiers: Name reservation acceptance notice
Signed Articles of Association
Sole shareholder decision and board resolution
Lease agreement and real property certificate
Foreign shareholder corporate existence certificate and legalisation copies
Identity and real-name verification records of directors, supervisor, legal representative
Establishment registration application form duly completed and signed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or returned with a rectification notice, the designated representative must correct the cited data within fifteen calendar days through the same online portal; if the review period expires, the application may be resubmitted as a continuation of the original file with no additional State fee. If the registry unreasonably refuses registration, the applicant may apply to the same office for administrative reconsideration within sixty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment information reporting and post-registration tax, banking, and labor filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local commerce department through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Reporting System, the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal, the People's Bank of China branch for foreign-exchange banking matters, and the local human resources and social security bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after receipt of the business license, complete the Foreign Investment Information Report, including final beneficial owner information and actual-controller data, on the one-window commerce reporting platform; no prior approval is required for non-negative-list activities. At the same time, complete tax registration and verification of the tax payer status, decide whether to apply for VAT general taxpayer status based on projected annual revenue, register the payroll and individual income tax withholding system, and complete social insurance and housing fund registrations. Open the company basic deposit account at a licensed bank and, if cross-border payment solutions such as Stripe or PayPal will be settled into the company, open or link a foreign-exchange settlement account and file the foreign-exchange business with the designated bank. If the company will directly engage in import or export of samples or returned goods, complete customs registration and obtain the customs declaration code; otherwise the entity may rely on licensed customs brokers for incidental shipments.
required_dossiers: Business license with Unified Social Credit Code
Articles of Association and shareholder decision
Foreign Investment Information Report data fields
Legal representative ID and bank signatory appointments
Lease contract for bank and tax address proof
Social insurance, individual income tax, and housing fund registration forms
Customs registration certificate only if direct import/export is contemplated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commerce department returns the investment information report for amendment, correct the affected data online within thirty days and certify the date and reason of correction. Any perceived tax registration default may be cured by filing late registration with a written explanation through the e-Tax portal before penalties are assessed, and the tax authority will normally accept voluntary correction if no fraudulent intent is shown.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety certification, environmental registration, and operational readiness for warehousing and fulfillment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Emergency Management Bureau / Fire and Rescue Section, local Ecology and Environment Bureau, and the Administration for Market Regulation for renewal of the business license if the scope is later expanded to on-site printing or manufacturing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the POD fulfillment warehouse or office is occupied and storage operations begin, submit an application for Fire Safety Inspection Filing to the local fire and rescue authority and arrange an on-site inspection of evacuation routes, exit signage, emergency lighting, fire extinguish equipment, smoke detectors or automatic sprinkler coverage, and the structural load certificate of the building. For ordinary non-hazardous apparel and packaging storage, no environmental impact assessment report is required, but file the environmental registration form with the local Ecology and Environment Bureau if the warehouse area is at or above the threshold in the local project classification list. If the company later operates in-house garment printing, heat-transfer presses, or solvent-based ink decoration on the premises, stop operations, apply under the printing industry regulations for a Printing Business Permit, install VOC abatement equipment, and obtain the appropriate pollutant discharge permit from the ecology authority. Conduct occupational safety registration with the county-level emergency management authority, appoint a part-time safety officer, and carry out hazard identification for the warehouse.
required_dossiers: Fire safety inspection application and building fire acceptance certificate
Structural load certificate and building ownership/lease records
Environmental registration form (only if threshold is met)
Printing permit and pollutant discharge permit (only if printing is added later)
Workplace safety production responsibility book
List of stored materials, packaging waste, batteries, and any flammable aerosols
Emergency response plan and fire drill record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety inspection fails, correct the listed deficiencies, request a re-inspection, and keep the warehouse closed until the certificate is issued; an administrative appeal may be lodged if the fire authority fails to act within the statutory period. For environmental registration queries, submit the revised registration online and pay any applicable nominal fee; if the government determines that a full EIA is required because of downstream printing operations, commission a licensed environmental impact assessment agency and continue the application without operating the printing line until approval is granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation for industrial and commercial licensing; local Emergency Management Bureau / Fire and Rescue Section for civil defense and fire permits; local Ecology and Environment Bureau for environmental impact assessment and pollutant discharge registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Market Entity Business License (establishment registration); Fire Safety Inspection Filing Acceptance Certificate for the fulfillment premises; Printing Business Permit and Pollutant Discharge Permit only if the company operates in-house printing or heat-transfer garment decoration. Pure print-on-demand retail and parcel fulfillment without in-house production require no separate manufacturing license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the provincial/municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau where the warehouse is registered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a pure retail fulfillment warehouse and office without garment printing, dyeing, or hazardous chemical storage, the project is Class III Environmental Registration Form or Exempt, depending on the local floor-area threshold. If the company installs on-site digital printing, heat-press, or solvent-based screen printing, the project moves to Class II requiring an Environmental Impact Report Form or a full Environmental Impact Report in sensitive zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must comply with GB/T 31962-2015: pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 400 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 45 mg/L. No industrial wastewater is generated from pure warehousing. If printing is added, VOC emissions must meet the local adoption of GB 16297-1996 and GB 37822-2019, including non-methane total hydrocarbons not exceeding 50 mg/m3 at organized exhaust outlets and no visible fugitive emissions; hazardous waste such as waste ink, solvent wipes, empty aerosol cans, and used cartridges must be segregated, stored in sealed leak-proof containers in a licensed hazardous waste storage area, and transported to a licensed disposal facility within one year, with manifest records retained for at least five years. General packaging waste must be recycled or disposed of by a licensed municipal waste operator.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the Fire Safety Inspection Filing Acceptance Certificate before occupancy, maintain with no less than one approved 4-kg ABC dry powder fire extinguisher per 200 square meters, verify that the maximum travel distance to an exit does not exceed 30 meters, and keep all emergency exits unobstructed. The building owner must provide a Structural Load Certificate confirming the floor can support finished apparel pallets and racking. Register the workplace in the local production safety supervision system, appoint a part-time safety management officer, prepare a fire and emergency evacuation plan, and conduct a fire drill at least once every six months. If employees work in a warehouse or operate heat-press equipment, file occupational hazard registration for noise and heat stress and provide appropriate personal protective equipment. A civil defense fire permit is required if any quantity of flammable inks, aerosol sprays, or lithium-battery apparel accessories is stored; the permitted storage quantity will be stated by the fire authority and must not be exceeded.

stage_2.extra_validated_notes: The business scope for ISIC 4791 is limited to internet retail, print-on-demand order management, custom apparel design, and parcel fulfillment. If production is wholly outsourced by the legal entity, no manufacturing licensing is mandated, but the fulfillment location in China triggers the warehouse fire-safety and environmental-registration duties described above. For a pure digital consulting firm without any physical premises, this licensing block would read as Not Applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (PRC); online electronic filing portal: the National Electronic Tax Bureau e-tax service platform operated by STA and its provincial tax bureaus (accessible from www.chinatax.gov.cn and the provincial e-tax gateways).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After the WFOE is incorporated, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues an 18-digit Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC), which automatically serves as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration number. No separate TIN application is required: tax registration is integrated into the business license. Within 30 days after issuance of the USCC, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax status registration in the electronic tax bureau including VAT taxpayer status, legal representative identity, equity structure, industry classification ISIC 4791, and banking details. The foreign parent company must provide notarised and legalised registration, a board resolution, and evidence of capital contribution to the SAMR during incorporation. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese permanent establishment, the procedure for obtaining a Chinese TIN consists of filing a non-resident enterprise tax registration with the competent STA office, submitting the home-country certificate of incorporation, a tax residence certificate, the appointment of the Chinese withholding agent or payer, and a description of the Chinese-source income; STA then issues a non-resident taxpayer identification number used solely for withholding and declaration purposes. A WFOE is, by default, a PRC resident taxpayer subject to entity-level taxation rather than a non-resident TIN holder.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide check-the-box, classification, or hybrid mismatch elections for a WFOE. A wholly foreign-owned limited liability company is compulsorily treated as a PRC resident enterprise for enterprise income tax purposes. No entity-level pass-through or transparent status is available. The small-scale VAT taxpayer status is an administrative indirect tax registration category, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) of the People's Republic of China
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All incorporated WFOEs must complete VAT registration together with tax registration immediately upon receipt of the USCC; there is no turnover threshold for basic VAT registration. For mandatory VAT general taxpayer classification, however, any enterprise whose taxable domestic sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 in a rolling 12-month period must be registered as a general VAT taxpayer. Export-oriented businesses may, and in practice must, apply for general VAT taxpayer registration regardless of turnover in order to claim 0% export VAT treatment and input VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The PRC mandates issuance of Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices (DEI) through STA's Electronic Tax Bureau platform. All newly formed enterprises, including WFOEs, are incorporated into the national electronic invoicing system and must transmit invoice data to the STA in real time at the moment of invoice issuance using STA-approved APIs or an STA-certified electronic invoice service provider. Each DEI carries a secure QR code and cryptographic digital signature generated by STA's central invoice issuance engine, with anti-fraud digital stamping replacing physical invoice sealing. For general VAT taxpayers, special VAT invoices remain subject to tax-control system matching and verification. Commodity and service tax classification codes are compulsory; e-commerce and Print-on-Demand platforms must ensure that every domestic sale is electronically invoiced at the applicable VAT rate, and that export sales are separately evidenced with customs and logistics proof for zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC VAT law, exported goods are zero-rated for VAT where: (i) the goods physically leave the customs territory of the PRC under a valid customs export declaration; (ii) the exporter is a VAT general taxpayer properly registered with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) as a customs exporter; (iii) the export value is supported by commercial, transport, and customs documentation; and (iv) the export-related foreign exchange proceeds are repatriated and recorded through licensed PRC banks in accordance with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) trade verification rules. Print-on-Demand custom apparel qualifies only if the completed garments are physically dispatched to an overseas buyer or destination outside mainland China; any portion sold for consumption in China remains subject to VAT at the standard rate. Qualifying cross-border services may also be zero-rated only if the service is within the published STA scope for zero-rated offshore services, is supplied to a non-resident overseas customer, is consumed entirely offshore, and is not connected with goods or services for use in China. Remote digital services rendered to consumers located within China are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration) filed through the China International Trade Single Window and accepted by the General Administration of Customs (GACC)
Commercial invoice evidencing the export value, HS code, buyer, consignee, and description of the POD apparel
Packing list reconciled with the export declaration and commercial invoice
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or express courier proof-of-export signed by the carrier

Export foreign exchange collection record or bank remittance certificate issued by a licensed PRC bank and verified in the SAFE cross-border trade system (the functional equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate, FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities will cross-check the customs export declaration, transport records, foreign exchange collection records, and VAT filing data. For any claimed zero-rating or VAT rebate found to be unsupported, falsified, or not backed by actual physical export and repatriated proceeds, the STA will claw back the VAT benefit, add late payment surcharge interest, and impose an administrative penalty ranging from one to five times the fraudulently obtained refund under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. If the conduct is intentional and material, it may constitute the criminal offense of fraudulent export tax refunds under the PRC Criminal Law. The exporter may also be disqualified from export VAT rebate treatment, have its VAT general taxpayer status reclassified, incur customs administrative penalties for false export declarations, and be subject to SAFE fines for export-proceeds non-repatriation or false collection records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the People's Republic of China (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate system with current-account convertibility and a regulated capital account. All bona fide trade- and service-related foreign currencies may be settled into RMB at designated foreign-exchange banks upon presentation of contracts, customs declarations, invoices and SAFE-monitored trade records. Capital-account transactions, however, remain strictly controlled: FDI subscriptions must obtain SAFE foreign-exchange registration and be remitted into a dedicated FDI capital account; subsequent conversion to RMB requires authenticity verification and is designated to permitted business uses. There is no statutory mandatory surrender ratio for current-account export receipts, but proceeds must be repatriated to China and either retained in foreign currency or settled through a domestic bank. Profit remittance by a WFOE is legally permissible after completion of annual audit, corporate income tax final settlement, and formal bank verification of audited financial statements and profit distribution resolution; practical hurdles include delayed SAFE registration updates, incomplete customs/tax documentation, and strict ultimate-beneficial-owner due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE goods-trade monitoring rules, export proceeds must be repatriated to China and enter a designated foreign-exchange bank within the trade contract period and, in any event, within the SAFE monitoring window normally not exceeding 90 days from the customs export declaration unless an approved extension or deferred payment arrangement is reported. No fixed mandatory conversion ratio applies; the exporter may retain the proceeds in a current-account foreign-currency settlement account or convert 100% to RMB at the bank's prevailing on-demand rate. For advance receipts exceeding USD 500,000 and more than 30 days before shipment, and for deferred receipts beyond 90 days after export, the exporter must file a supplementary report through the bank for SAFE balance-of-payments monitoring.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a standalone clearing solution. Financial technology EMIs are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in China and may not clear RMB or hold customer funds in domestic bank accounts. A WFOE cannot rely on an offshore EMI for statutory account opening, FDI capital injection, or export proceeds collection. Such providers may act only as a software or acquiring layer integrated with a licensed domestic bank or a cross-border payment institution holding a PBOC non-bank payment license; all funds must ultimately enter or leave through SAFE-supervised bank rails. Stripe and PayPal therefore require local integration: PayPal through its licensed China subsidiary and domestic bank settlement, and Stripe through a licensed cross-border payment facilitator or a Hong Kong affiliate, neither of which replaces a mainland Tier-1 commercial bank treasury relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under PBOC account-opening and AML rules, a newly formed WFOE must complete an in-branch KYC interview. The statutory legal representative, who may also be the sole director, must appear physically at the chosen bank branch with original identity documents, corporate chops, and board resolutions. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted as a standalone method for first-time account establishment. Where the legal representative is an offshore non-resident, some Tier-1 banks will accept a notarized and legalized power of attorney in favor of a local financial officer together with a bank-arranged remote video interview, but the account remains subject to branch-level compliance sign-off and a period of transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO traceability gap: ultimate individual ownership is not transparent, contains shell layers, or diverges from the municipal market supervision registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation, amended articles of association, signed shareholder structure chart covering every intermediary entity down to each natural person, notarized passports of all beneficial owners, source-of-wealth statements with tax returns and bank statements, negative PEP declarations, and a corporate veil waterfall memorandum for the bank compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency fragmented cross-border receipts from Stripe/PayPal that do not match the declared POD retail business model and may be perceived as structuring or money smurfing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform payout and settlement reports from Stripe/PayPal, order-level transaction logs, e-commerce store URLs, refund chargeback ledgers, delivery tracking records, customs e-commerce export declaration records, and a written reconciliation model explaining daily settlement volatility and average ticket size.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade documentation mismatch: bill-of-lading or customs declaration values are lower than bank receipt amounts, suggesting over-invoicing, double invoicing, or undisclosed service fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full sales contracts, purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or air waybills, electronic China customs export declarations, third-party inspection certificates, insurance certificates, supplier/vendor registration documents, and independent logistics tracking proving physical delivery of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance failure: the WFOE appears to have no physical office, employees, or operational capacity, raising shell-entity risk despite low-risk retail classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tenancy lease or property ownership certificate, utility and property-management invoices, payroll records and social insurance contribution filings for staff, office photographs and geotagged video walkthrough, corporate income tax returns, VAT invoices, business license, and a third-party business verification report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investor executes board resolutions and a capital contribution agreement, then obtains SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration through the selected Tier-1 bank. The WFOE opens a dedicated FDI capital account at the bank, and the overseas parent remits equity funds via SWIFT MT103 using the SAFE transaction classification code for direct-investment equity capital, referencing the FDI registration contract number. Upon receipt, the bank performs authenticity verification and registers the inflow in SAFE's capital project monitoring system. After conversion to RMB in a capital settlement account, a Chinese certified public accountant issues a Capital Verification Report. Settled capital may only be used for current operating expenditures such as inventory procurement, salaries, rent, marketing, and approved business investments; it cannot be used for entrusted loans, equity investment outside the approved scope, or speculative financial products without separate SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw-material and supplier payments, the WFOE uses either RMB or foreign-currency clearing through its SAFE-designated domestic bank. Open-account settlement is executed via SWIFT MT103 with the applicable current-account trade purpose code and is supported by import contracts, commercial invoices, purchase orders, and customs import declarations where required. For high-value or credit-supported purchases, the bank issues an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit via SWIFT MT700, with negotiation through correspondent banks under UCP600. Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) may be used for lower-value or counterparty-controlled shipments, with the collecting bank releasing documents against payment or acceptance. All outbound FX purchases and debits must align with SAFE goods-trade supervision, pricing consistency checks, and the bank's country-risk and counterparty KYC policies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a domestic Tier-1 bank for genuine current-account trade receipts and payments, supported by underlying contracts and limited to a maturity not exceeding 12 months
Vanilla FX call and put options, including zero-premium collars, used to hedge forecasted trade exposures and subject to the bank's real-demand test
Cross-currency swaps only for approved capital-account liabilities such as registered foreign debt, with SAFE filing and no speculative swap overlay

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore settlements; onshore entities must use deliverable RMB forwards, and any NDF exposure must be converted into deliverable onshore hedging instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (Annual Report) to the State Administration for Market Regulation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 immediately after the reporting calendar year (January 1 - December 31); no staggered or anniversary deadline extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing within the June 30 window results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises Operating Abnormally within 10 working days; failure continuing for 3 consecutive years leads to entry in the List of Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, public credit blacklisting, restriction of the legal representative from new market registrations, and possible administrative revocation/strike-off of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Final Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration responsible for the WFOE's tax registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 immediately following the tax year; the statutory tax year runs January 1 - December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late settlement incurs daily overdue interest of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the due date; failure to file draws a non-filing penalty of up to RMB 2,000 (or up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases); underpayment arising from fraudulent or false declarations is subject to an administrative penalty of 50% - 500% of the underpaid tax and potential criminal liability for serious tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investment Information Reporting for WFOE status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation jointly with the Ministry of Commerce via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 immediately after the reporting year, filed concurrently with the Annual Enterprise Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit timely, accurate, and complete foreign investment information triggers a rectification order from the commerce department; refusal to rectify may incur an administrative fine up to RMB 200,000 in serious cases and an adverse market-credit record that can impair cross-border foreign-exchange and financing facilitation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statements Audit by a PRC Licensed CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting/board of directors; audited statements retained in the corporate record and available to the State Administration for Market Regulation and tax authorities upon inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completion and presentation before the annual shareholders' meeting, and in all cases before reliance for the June 30 annual enterprise report filing; local practice commonly requires the audit to be completed within 4 months after the December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of the compulsory annual audit requirement under the PRC Company Law exposes directors and supervisors to liability, makes the annual report potentially incomplete for credit and tax purposes, and can lead to an administrative order to correct; knowingly publishing or delivering misleading audit-based financial materials is punishable under the PRC Accounting Law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative exemption threshold exists. Under PRC Company Law, every limited-liability enterprise, including a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, must engage an independent PRC-licensed certified public accountant to audit its annual financial statements regardless of balance-sheet size, turnover, or headcount. For accounting-standard classification, a small enterprise is defined as total assets of not more than RMB 30 million, annual turnover of not more than RMB 30 million, and fewer than 300 employees; breaching any of those three quantitative indicators requires full PRC GAAP presentation. The statutory audit mandate still applies below those thresholds, so a dormant zero-revenue WFOE remains required to procure an audit opinion.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC GAAP/CAS), substantially converged with IFRS, plus the PRC Accounting Law; a WFOE that qualifies as a small enterprise may prepare under the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but a separate IFRS or US GAAP package may be required by the foreign parent for consolidation and cannot replace the PRC statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Mainland China has no UK-style annual UBO confirmation or public ultimate-beneficial-owner register. The WFOE meets annual reporting obligations through the Annual Enterprise Information Report and the Annual Foreign Investment Information Report, which disclose shareholders, capital contributions, and ultimate-controller structures. Any share transfer, director change, registered-capital change, or other registered-item alteration must be registered with the local SAMR within 30 days after the change; foreign-investment information changes are reported at the same registration window or within 20 working days through the enterprise registration system. Beneficial-ownership verification also applies in bank/KYC files but is not filed with the companies registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,800 per annum for a Tier-1 city registered address and corporate agent; lower-tier cities may be USD 250 - USD 900 per annum
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 5,000 for a small/medium POD WFOE; groups requiring parent-consolidation confirming reports under IFRS may incur USD 5,000 - USD 15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for High-New Technology Enterprises; reduced small-low-profit enterprise rates (effective tax burden of 5% or 10% for qualifying taxable income ≤ RMB 3 million); 100% super-deduction for qualified R&D expenses; potential regional incentives such as 15% rate for enterprises in Western China Development Zone and Hainan Free Trade Port if business qualifies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Class) for enterprises subject to deemed accounting; filed via the State Taxation Administration e-Tax Portal (chinatax.gov.cn).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly estimated prepayments filed within 15 days of each quarter-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing and final settlement must be completed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by May 31 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales Revenue – gross revenue from selling print-on-demand custom apparel, including all domestic and cross-border e-commerce sales settled via Stripe and PayPal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue sourced worldwide since the WFOE is a PRC tax resident. Ensure foreign-currency sales are translated at the applicable exchange rate; do not net out payment-processor fees or refunds unless separately permitted. Cross-border sales to non-resident customers must be supported by transportation and payment records to substantiate the underlying transaction and any VAT/consumption tax adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Sales – direct costs of production, including raw materials, printing supplies, sublimation coatings, packaging, and direct labour.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If related-party purchases (e.g., from the foreign parent or an overseas affiliate) are used, the pricing must comply with the arm's length standard; any transfer pricing adjustment will increase taxable income. Do not deduct customs duties or VAT that is creditable. Imported goods must have proper customs declarations and supporting documents for the cost claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, Administrative and Financial Expenses – including online marketplace commissions (e.g., Etsy/Amazon), payment processor fees, marketing costs, rent, salaries, and interest expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to non-residents for services or digital advertising may attract withholding tax (10% for service fees or deemed profit basis) and must be reported separately. Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is deductible only if it meets the arm's length interest rate and the debt-to-equity ratio (statutory thin capitalization limit 2:1 or 5:1 for financial institutions); otherwise the excess is non-deductible. Ensure that any cross-border service contract is properly documented and that the service provider retains economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Profit – accounting operating profit after deducting operating costs and all period expenses from revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the pre-tax accounting profit before non-operating items. If the WFOE received intercompany management fees from overseas entities, verify that the fee is at arm's length and that the recipient has relevant functions, assets, and risks. For POD operations, ensure proper allocation of costs between China and any overseas fulfillment centers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Accounting Profit – profit before tax including non-operating income and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose any foreign exchange gains/losses from receivables/payables denominated in USD/EUR, as well as any subsidies or grants from the government. If the WFOE derives income from overseas branches or subsidiaries, include the attributable profit or loss subject to PRC enterprise income tax; foreign tax credits for overseas income taxes are claimed separately in Line 21.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjustments – net increase/decrease adjustments to convert accounting profit to taxable income. Common adjustments include transfer pricing, thin capitalization, non-deductible withholding taxes, advertising limits, and R&D super-deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any outbound dividend, interest, or royalty payments that were subject to Chinese withholding tax (10% statutory, possibly reduced by DTA) cannot be deducted as tax expenses inside the income tax return. Transfer pricing adjustments between the WFOE and overseas related parties must be filed as a taxable increase. If the company enjoyed treaty benefits (e.g., 5% WHT on dividends), ensure that the beneficial ownership documentation and TRC are retained for inspection; any mischaracterization will lead to full uplift and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income – after applying net tax adjustments and carrying forward prior-year losses (up to 5 years, or 10 years for High-New Technology enterprises).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE operating as a POD retailer, typical adjustments relate to marketing spend exceeding 15% of gross sales, entertainment expenses exceeding 60% of actual expenditure subject to maximum caps, and non-deductible payments to non-residents lacking proper documentation. Loss carryforward eligibility must be evidenced by a tax audit or filing history; any sudden change in ownership or business purpose may be challenged under anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Tax Payable – taxable income multiplied by the statutory 25% corporate income tax rate (or preferential rate, e.g., 15% for High-New Technology Enterprise or 5%/10% effective small-low-profit rates).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is treated as a small-low-profit enterprise based on its employees, assets, and taxable income, it must compute at the reduced effective rates. Note: the small-low-profit preference generally does not apply to overseas-controlled entities unless all statutory conditions are met; verify that the entity is in active POD retailing. For High-New Technology, the WFOE must hold a valid high-tech certificate to access the 15% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Deductions and Credits – including relief for preferential tax rates, equipment accelerated depreciation, and foreign income tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for income earned from foreign POD sales (taxes paid in the destination jurisdiction) are capped at the PRC tax payable on the same foreign-source income. The credit is limited to the amount of PRC tax attributable to that income; excess credits cannot be carried back or forward except as allowed by regulation. For royalties paid to a foreign licensor, the PRC withholding tax paid must not be claimed as an income tax credit in the WFOE's own return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid Tax – quarterly estimated tax payments made during the year (each 25% of the annual projected tax or based on actual quarterly profit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The quarterly prepayments must be made via the e-Tax portal within 15 days after each quarter-end. If the WFOE failed to prepay due to late recognition of online sales revenue, interest and late-payment penalties may be assessed from the due date. Under-forecast prepayments do not automatically trigger penalties if the final settlement shows a minimal balance, but intentional underpayment may be treated as evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Tax Due or Refund – the difference between income tax payable and the sum of prepayments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE owes tax, payment must be made by the filing deadline (May 31); any overdue balance accrues a daily late-payment interest at 0.05% per annum. If a refund is due, it will be processed after tax authority verification; requests for refunds on cross-border withholding mismatches require submission of corrected withholding forms and exchange-rate evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file annual corporate income tax return by May 31 triggers a RMB 2,000 fine (or up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases) under Article 62 of the Law on Administration of Tax Collection (LATC); moreover, overdue tax attracts daily surcharges of 0.05% of the unpaid tax per day from the statutory deadline. Underpayment arising from false or fraudulent claims (e.g., overstating exempt revenue) may be deemed tax evasion under LATC Article 63, leading to penalties of 50%–500% of the evaded tax and criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 (imprisonment up to seven years for large-scale evasion).
